question: Which government passed the Aparajita Women and Child Bill, 2024, in September 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**West Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Aparajita Women and Child Bill, 2024, was passed by the Government of West Bengal in September 2024.
 
• The Bill aims to ensure the protection and empowerment of women and children in the state.
 
• It includes provisions for the safety, education, and health of women and children.
 
• The legislation focuses on creating a supportive environment for women and children, particularly those from marginalized communities.
 
• West Bengal has been proactive in implementing policies for women's and children's welfare, with several initiatives already in place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Women's Safety in India**

 
 
• Women's safety has been a critical issue in India, with various laws and measures implemented to address it.
 
• The Nirbhaya Fund was established in 2013 to support initiatives aimed at enhancing the safety and security of women.
 
• Several states have launched helplines and mobile apps to offer immediate assistance to women in distress.
 
• Public awareness campaigns and self-defense training programs are also part of efforts to ensure women's safety.
 
 
 
• **Child Welfare Policies**
 
 
• India has implemented several policies to safeguard children's rights, including the Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS).
 
• The Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009 mandates free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• Anganwadi centers under the Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme provide nutrition, health, and education services to children under six years of age.
 
• The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 focuses on the care and protection of children in conflict with the law and those in need of care and protection.
 
 
 
• **Women's Empowerment Initiatives**
 
 
• Various schemes such as Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana, and Mahila E-Haat aim to empower women economically and socially.
 
• The Self-Help Group (SHG) movement has been instrumental in empowering rural women through microfinance and entrepreneurship.
 
• The National Mission for Empowerment of Women (NMEW) works towards inter-sectoral convergence of all programs related to women's welfare and empowerment.
 
• Skill development programs like Skill India and PMKVY offer training to women in various trades to enhance their employability.
 
 
 
• **Healthcare Initiatives for Women and Children**
 
 
• Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) promotes institutional deliveries to reduce maternal and neonatal mortality.
 
• Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) aims to improve the overall health of children from birth to 18 years.
 
• Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) provides financial assistance to pregnant and lactating mothers for their first living child.
 
• Mission Indradhanush focuses on full immunization coverage for children and pregnant women.
